A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LinGen research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary materials are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LinGen training experiments, VBench evaluations, human preference comparisons, latency measurements, and ablations in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a computed token-adjacency diagnostic in supplementary Appendix A and Figure 13.

M1.justification: The MATE architecture, bidirectional Mamba2, Rotary-Major Scan, review tokens, TESA, and training procedures are retained. The added adjacency analysis evaluates the existing design without modifying it.

E1.justification: Shutterstock and RawFilm training coverage, video-generation tasks, and VBench-Long, standard, and custom evaluations remain unchanged. The new token-distance diagnostic does not introduce another video dataset or generation task.

E2.justification: v1 Appendix A names T2V-Turbo, whereas v2 Appendix B names T2V-Turbo-v2. However, the corresponding citation, example images, and human-comparison figures remain unchanged and still identify T2V-Turbo. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a comparator substitution or a labeling correction; other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new adjacency diagnostic uses a 32 × 32 × 32 token tensor, neighborhoods within 2 × 2 × 2 cubes, and minimum distances across 1-12 layers. Existing training budgets, VBench protocols, and human-comparison settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused structural analysis comparing adjacency preservation for vanilla Mamba, RMS/Zigzag, and RMS with TESA. This supplements the retained loss-curve, latency, human-evaluation, and visual ablations.

E5.justification: Both retain Figure 9's statement that human-evaluation variance is 3%, without changes to run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The new averaged token-distance metric is not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Figure 13 reports that RMS/Zigzag reaches an average minimum distance of 1 by four layers, while RMS with TESA achieves 1 from the first layer and vanilla Mamba remains much higher. Existing benchmark scores, human preferences, latency values, and training-loss results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A introduces d_k, the average minimum sequence distance between neighboring tokens across k layers, as a mathematical diagnostic. Existing scan definitions and FLOPs equations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about linear complexity, minute-length generation on one GPU, video quality, and efficiency. The new appendix supplies support for an existing claim rather than expanding its scope.

C2.justification: The new appendix links minimum token distance across layers to correlation precision and interprets the diagnostic as explaining how RMS and TESA preserve adjacency. Existing interpretations of video quality and limitations of VBench are retained.

D1.justification: The supplementary demo-access instructions change from opening a local index.html file to consulting the project website. Architecture details, hyperparameters, dataset-selection procedures, hardware information, and Table 7's training recipe are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to DiM: Diffusion Mamba for Efficient High-Resolution Image Synthesis and Diffusion Models Without Attention, with brief positioning of earlier SSM image-generation work in Appendix E.2. It removes the Nerfies citation previously acknowledging the website template.

P1.justification: v2 adds the opening Adjacency Preservation appendix, a main-text cross-reference, and a short prior-work explanation. Existing appendix sections are renumbered from A-D to B-E; most wording and narrative organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 13, redraws the efficiency plots, adjusts plot legends, reverses Table 1's metric-block order, and reformats Table 2 into explicit component columns. Existing supplementary figures are retained and renumbered, with accompanying text reflow.

improvement.justification: The adjacency diagnostic adds concrete support to v1's explanation of RMS and TESA, while the component-based Table 2 clarifies the ablations and added references improve attribution. These are limited gains because the main experimental evidence is unchanged and the diagnostic covers one tensor setting. The T2V-Turbo version-label ambiguity is a small clarity drawback.
